key_insight: Photonic variational circuits are trainable for a broad class of low-order photon-number observables, but high-order and probability-based observables typically become sample-inefficient, often exponentially so.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical rule for designing near-term photonic quantum models: choose observables and losses that keep sample cost polynomial to make training feasible at scale.
method: Defined trainability using the ratio of sample variance to circuit variance.
Analyzed photon-number observables in passive linear-optical quantum circuits.
Separated observables into polynomial-sample and exponential-sample regimes, including cases where quantum estimation outperforms classical methods.
evidence_signal: The paper combines analytic results with numerically observed polynomial decay of circuit variance to support the scaling claims.
watch_item: Trainability depends strongly on observable choice, so implementations using high-order moments or output probabilities may still face prohibitive sampling costs.
paper_title: The trainability of photonic quantum circuits
